why: Pain is a real protective experience influenced by the body, nervous system, context, expectations, emotions, and past learning.

slides.title: Pain Is Real
slides.content: Pain is not imaginary. It is a protective experience produced by a complex nervous system using information from many sources.

slides.title: Context Can Matter
slides.content: Symptoms can be influenced by injury, health, sleep, stress, beliefs, environment, memory, and what an activity means to you.

slides.title: Pain Is Not a Damage Meter
slides.content: Pain can be intense without providing a precise measure of tissue damage. This does not mean symptoms should be dismissed or that every activity is automatically safe.

slides.title: Learning Can Change
slides.content: Supportive education and carefully chosen activity may help some people build confidence and function. The plan should fit the person and presentation.

slides.title: Ask a Better Question
slides.content: Instead of asking only ‘How much does it hurt?’, also ask ‘What can I do, what matters to me, and what response would be sensible today?’
